You need Wi-Fi and Android 11 or newer. Pairing is done once; after the phone restarts you only repeat step 7.

1. Connect the phone to Wi-Fi.

2. Turn on Developer options: Settings › About phone › Software information › tap “Build number” 7 times. (On other phones: Settings › About phone › Build number.)

3. Open Shizuku. If it asks to show notifications, allow it: the pairing code is typed in a Shizuku notification.

4. In Shizuku, under “Start via Wireless debugging”, tap “Pairing”. On the page that opens, tap “Developer options”, turn on “Wireless debugging” and confirm “Allow”.

5. Tap the words “Wireless debugging” (not the switch), then “Pair device with pairing code”. A 6-digit code appears.

6. Keep that screen open and pull down the notifications. When Shizuku's notification says “Pairing service found”, tap “Enter pairing code” and type the code. Shizuku says pairing succeeded.

7. Go back to Shizuku and tap “Start” under “Start via Wireless debugging”. Wait until it says “Shizuku is running”.

8. Come back to Waaiya and tap “Give permission”, then “Allow”.

After a phone restart Shizuku stops: connect to Wi-Fi, turn “Wireless debugging” back on if it is off, open Shizuku and tap “Start”. No new pairing.
Four short steps, done once. No extra app and no computer. Waaiya ticks each step when it is done.

Android hides the text of notifications while an app captures the screen, and filtering counts as one. Waaiya can turn off this protection while it filters, and turns it back on when filtering stops.\n\nWhile it is off, a screen share at the same time (a video call, for example) can also show your notifications and codes to others.

Open Waaiya and do the one-time setup again (Wireless debugging, Shizuku or a computer). It now also allows this tile. On Xiaomi phones, turn on “USB debugging (Security settings)” in Developer options first.
The one-time setup on this phone, with pictures. The pictures come from one phone: on yours the menus may look a little different, but the names are the same.
Turn on Developer options: in Settings › About phone, tap “Build number” 7 times (on some phones it is under Software information). Skip this if Developer options are already on.
In Waaiya, on the Setup page, tap “Open Developer options”. Waaiya opens Developer options and shows a notification.
Scroll down to “Wireless debugging” (under Debugging) and tap its name, not the switch.
Turn on “Use wireless debugging” and confirm with “Allow”.
A 6-digit code appears. Keep this screen open.
Pull down the notifications. In Waaiya\'s notification, tap “Enter code”.
Type the 6 digits and tap send.
Waaiya finishes by itself and says “Setup done”. You can now turn Wireless debugging off, unless Waaiya says it uses its helper on your phone.

• Cannot find a menu: use the search at the top of Settings and type “Build number” or “Wireless debugging”.
• Wireless debugging needs Wi-Fi (internet is not needed). Without Wi-Fi it does not turn on.
• No “Enter code” in the notification (notifications are off for Waaiya, or the phone hides the field): open Settings and Waaiya side by side (split screen) and tap “Type the code here” in Waaiya.
• The code was not accepted: it changes each time the pairing screen opens. Open it again and type the new code.
